beats: Goosebumps keep you warm. Everyone knows that. Everyone except your body.
When you get cold, tiny muscles pull each hair upright. If you were furry, that fluffed-up fur would trap warm air.
But you're not furry anymore. So you just get bumpy skin. For nothing.
Same with fear. Animals puff up to look bigger. Cats do it. Dogs do it. Your body still tries, with no fur to puff.
So goosebumps don't keep you warm. They're leftover fur software, running on naked hardware. Follow Why Why Why for the why behind everything.
